pages.text: "Sonu, let's go up!" Mina, a handspan taller, called from the lowest step. Low river water came only to their ankles. Mom rinsed a towel beside them.
Mina wanted to climb beside Sonu. Breakfast waited on the platform above. But round-bellied little Sonu loved water play and would not move. "Hurry! I'm hungry!"
Mina wrapped their trunk around Sonu's and pulled hard. "Waaah!" Sonu cried. Mina kept looking only at the platform above.
Sonu sat on the wet step, sobbing. Mom quickly lifted Sonu to a dry step. Mina stood alone below.
Mom gently linked her trunk with Mina's, light as hooking a thread. No pulling, only linking. "Oh? It doesn't hurt." Mina's eyes widened.
Mina approached Sonu. "Sorry I pulled hard. May I link gently?" Sonu nodded, and Mina softly linked their trunks.
Sonu stopped crying and giggled. Following the linked trunk, Sonu climbed one step, then two. Without a pull, Sonu followed.
Mom said, "From here, unlink and climb one step at a time." Mina unlinked and stood behind Sonu. Mom walked beside them.
Both reached dry ground at the top. Mina looked back at Sonu. "We came slowly, and both made it."
Mom drew both children into her arms. Mina smiled at Sonu. "Let's have breakfast now."
